what_happened: The request for job 20261025-001236-brde listed the study site generator as one of the readers of records/. The operator wrote that from memory. The generator actually reads studies/, not records/. The accepted reading turned this into a criterion that could not be met. The planning critic kept finding the problem, and planning failed after three rounds. The job was then stopped by an intervention.
cause: Nothing in intake treats a code fact in a request (which module reads which directory) as a claim to verify. The reading is accepted as written and criteria are built on it. The contradiction with the code only shows up when the critic examines the plan, and three planning rounds are spent trying to satisfy a criterion that cannot hold.
prevention: Add a reading-acceptance check that pulls out every code path, file, reader or consumer named in the request or in a criterion. It resolves each one against the current snapshot, for example by searching for the directory or symbol the named component reads. A name that does not resolve, or a stated relationship that the code contradicts, such as "the site generator reads records/", is flagged. The flagged items are returned to the requester or removed from the reading before planning starts.
proposed_request: Add a check to reading acceptance that resolves the code facts named in a request before planning starts. Outcome: when a request or an accepted criterion names a code path, file, module or reader, and says what it reads or writes (for example "the study site generator reads records/"), Athena looks that claim up in the current snapshot. If the named item is missing, or the code contradicts the stated relationship, the reading is not accepted. The requester sees which claims failed, and what the code shows in their place. Acceptance: (1) a test with a request that says the study site generator reads records/ (it reads studies/) is refused with a message naming the correct directory; (2) a test with a request whose named paths and readers all match the code is accepted unchanged; (3) the check runs before any planning round; (4) the check does not itself rewrite the reading.
